result.notes:
SCOPE COVERED (all clean unless listed above)
Main sweep: 2190 paired comparisons = 6 argv (['--help'], [], ['--val','5'], ['--key','a'], ['--key','a','--val','1','extra'], ['--bogus']) x 365 env variants:
- COLUMNS = every integer 1..120 inclusive -> 720 comparisons, ALL IDENTICAL. Every wrap regime is exercised (1-col degenerate, the <=17 fully-broken band, the 20s/30s partial-usage wraps, the 75%-prog-name threshold, the help-column collapse, and >=50 single-line).
- COLUMNS = 0, -1, -5, -80, 100000, 99999999999999999999, 'abc', 'wide', '40abc', 'abc40', '  40  ', '\t40\t', '\n40\n', ' 40', '40 ', '+40', '-0', '40.0', '40.', '0x28', '0b101000', '040', '', ' ', '\t', 'NaN', 'Infinity', 'inf', '1e2', NBSP-padded, thin-space-padded, \v/\f-padded -> ALL IDENTICAL.
- COLUMNS unset entirely -> IDENTICAL.
- LINES alone with COLUMNS unset (1, 2, 10, 24, 25, 1000, 0, -1, 'abc', '', '  24  ') -> ALL IDENTICAL. LINES correctly has no effect on width in either binary.
- LINES x COLUMNS cross product (11 LINES x 18 COLUMNS x 6 argv = 1188) -> only the '4_0' cell diverged; LINES never changes the outcome.
Additional: 49 targeted Unicode/whitespace probes, a 200-width fingerprint oracle used to recover each binary's effective numeric width, a 96-case confirmation sweep, 10 bash/byte-level spot checks, and the built-in difftest battery (162/162 identical).

SINGLE ROOT CAUSE
All findings are the same function: parseIntStrict in /output/lib/python/terminal.mjs, which stands in for CPython's int(os.environ['COLUMNS']):
    const text = raw.trim();
    if (!/^[+-]?\d+$/.test(text)) return 0;
    return Number.parseInt(text, 10);
Three deviations from int(str): (1) no PEP 515 single-underscore-between-digits support; (2) \d is ASCII-only whereas int() accepts any Unicode category-Nd digit; (3) String.prototype.trim() and CPython's int() whitespace set are not equal in both directions.

FIXING (3) NEEDS CARE - do not just swap in CPython's str.strip() set. Empirically probed against the reference: U+0085 and U+00A0 and the Zs/Zl/Zp separators ARE accepted, but the C0 separators \x1c \x1d \x1e \x1f are NOT (both binaries already agree and fall back on those - a naive "use str.strip semantics" fix would introduce a new divergence there). U+FEFF, U+200B and U+180E must be rejected.

LATENT, NOT OBSERVABLE
COLUMNS='1_0_0' hits the same underscore bug (reference resolves 100, port 80) but both widths are wide enough that the rendered bytes are identical, so it is not a reportable divergence today - it would become one if the help text ever grew.

NO CONSTRAINT VIOLATIONS
grep over all of /output for Map / new Map / WeakMap / Set / new Set / WeakSet / require( / module.exports returns zero matches. All files are .mjs with fully suffixed relative imports and no external deps.

Throwaway scripts (all under /tmp, nothing in /output or /workspace/dataset was touched): /tmp/fuzz/run.mjs (main sweep), /tmp/fuzz/run2.mjs (confirmation sweep), /tmp/fuzz/probe.mjs (Unicode spelling probes), /tmp/fuzz/oracle.mjs (effective-width oracle), /tmp/fuzz/dump.mjs, /tmp/fuzz/dump2.mjs, /tmp/fuzz/nel.sh, /tmp/fuzz/failures.json, /tmp/fuzz/failures2.json.

divergences.summary: U+2FFC IDEOGRAPHIC DESCRIPTION CHARACTER (one of U+2FFC..U+2FFF): the reference escapes it as non-printable (⿼), the port emits it raw. Root cause is Unicode-version skew — /output/lib/python/unicode_props.mjs asks the *runtime's* ICU for \p{Cn} (Node 18 / ICU 74 = Unicode 15.1) while the reference CPython carries Unicode 15.0, where these code points are still unassigned. The divergent set is exactly the 627 code points added in Unicode 15.1: U+2FFC..U+2FFF, U+31EF, U+2EBF0..U+2EE5D (verified boundaries: U+2FFB, U+31EE, U+2EBEF and U+2EE5E all match). Fix: pin an explicit Unicode 15.0 printability table (or add these 627 code points to the non-printable set) instead of relying on RegExp Unicode property escapes.

result.notes:
SCOPE / SNAPSHOT. /output was being edited while I worked (argv.mjs appeared at 05:06, test2.mjs at 05:07). I discarded the first round of results and re-ran every suite against a stable snapshot: md5 over `find /output -name '*.mjs' | sort | xargs md5sum | md5sum` = e38f082198265d827ec566c04db33c50, identical before and after the final runs. All numbers below are for that snapshot.

WHAT I RAN (8,976 differential comparisons, >6,000 distinct --key values). Throwaway scripts, all under /tmp/fz (nothing under /output or /workspace/dataset was touched):
- /tmp/fz/harness.mjs — concurrent spawn-both-and-compare (stdout+stderr+exit status, only [PYI-<pid>:ERROR] normalized).
- /tmp/fz/sweep.mjs — EXHAUSTIVE sweep of every code point U+0001..U+10FFFF except surrogates (1,112,033 code points), batched 512 per --key string, then every code point of any failing batch re-tested individually. 1,148 + 3,584 = 4,732 runs. This is the strongest evidence: the divergent set is exactly 627 code points and nothing else in the whole code point space differs.
- /tmp/fz/curated.mjs — 439 distinct hand-built keys: quotes (', ", '', "", '", "', a'b, a"b, a'b"c, ''', """, curly/guillemet quotes), backslashes (1/2/3/4 in a row, leading/trailing, \n \t \x41 A \U00000041 literals, Windows paths), ALL C0 controls U+0001..U+001F, U+007F, ALL C1 U+0080..U+009F, soft hyphen U+00AD, U+2028/U+2029, every Zs (U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000..U+200A, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000, U+180E), zero-width/format (U+200B/C/D, U+FEFF, U+2060..U+2065, U+061C, U+0600, U+13430, U+1BCA0, U+1D173, U+E0001, U+E0020, U+E007F), combining marks (U+0300..U+0308, U+0327, U+0334, U+035C, U+0483, U+0591, U+064B, U+0903, U+093C, U+0E31, U+20E3, U+20DD, U+FE00, U+FE0F, U+1AB0, U+1DC0, stacked diacritics), RTL/bidi (U+200E/F, U+202A..U+202E, U+2066..U+2069, Arabic/Hebrew text), non-ASCII printable (accented Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, CJK, Hangul, kana, Thai, Devanagari, symbols), astral/emoji incl. skin-tone modifiers, ZWJ families (👨‍👩‍👧‍👦, 👨‍❤️‍💋‍👨), flag sequences (🇺🇸, 🇯🇵, tag-sequence 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿), lone regional indicators, keycaps, noncharacters (U+FFFE/F, U+FDD0, U+1FFFE, U+10FFFE), private use (U+E000, U+F8FF, U+F0000, U+100000), unassigned (U+0378, U+0530, U+05EB, U+FFF0), Unicode 14.0/15.0/15.1/16.0 additions, and ~20 multi-char mixes combining all of the above.
- /tmp/fz/singles.mjs — 2,252 runs: every single code point U+0001..U+07FF individually, all 2-char combinations over {a,b,A,B,c,space,tab,newline,0,',\,soft-hyphen,ZWSP}, and a/b wrapped in every invisible.
- /tmp/fz/bytefuzz.mjs — 1,181 runs with RAW argv bytes built by bash printf so invalid UTF-8 reaches execve: every single byte 0x01..0xFF as the whole key, 900 deterministic-random 2..6-byte strings, plus hand-picked truncated/overlong/CESU-8/5- and 6-byte/F5-FF sequences. ZERO divergences — the port's /output/lib/python/argv.mjs re-reads /proc/self/cmdline and applies PEP 383 surrogateescape, so lone surrogates print identically (e.g. byte 0x80 -> KeyError: '\udc80' on both sides). NOTE: an earlier snapshot of the port (before argv.mjs existed) failed all of these with U+FFFD; that is fixed in the verified snapshot.
- /tmp/fz/forms.mjs — 193 runs: repr-sensitive keys passed as a separate argv element (--key VALUE) and in reversed option order, 5000-char and 2000-emoji keys, 1000 consecutive quotes/backslashes, plus env variations (COLUMNS=1/200, LC_ALL=C, LANG=C, LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8, PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8, PYTHONUTF8=0/1, TERM=dumb) and cwd variations (/, /tmp, /workspace). Zero divergences.
- /tmp/fz/bounds.mjs — 14 boundary probes pinning the divergent range exactly.
- /tmp/fz/nul.mjs — NUL is not passable: Node's spawn rejects it ("must be a string without null bytes") for both binaries, and via /bin/sh the shell drops it, after which BOTH sides report KeyError: 'ab'. No divergence; NUL is unreachable through argv on Linux.
- /workspace/verify/difftest.mjs built-in battery: 162/162 identical.

SUCCESS SET CONFIRMED. Across all single code points U+0001..U+07FF, all 2-char combinations over that alphabet, a/b padded with every invisible, and the 439 curated keys, the reference exits 0 for exactly two keys: 'a' (stdout "1\n") and 'b' (stdout "2\n"). Everything else exits 1 with a KeyError traceback, and the port agrees on every one of them. No normalization/folding leaks in either direction (fullwidth ａ, Cyrillic а, 'á' precomposed vs decomposed, 𝐚, ⓐ, 'a' + ZWSP/soft-hyphen/BOM/U+0301 all correctly fail).

REPR RULES THAT WERE VERIFIED CORRECT. Quote selection (single quotes by default, double quotes iff the string contains ' and not "; ' escaped only under single quotes), \\ escaping, the \t \n \r special cases, \xhh for C0/DEL/C1, \uXXXX for BMP non-printables, \UXXXXXXXX for astral non-printables, U+0020 treated as printable while all other Zs are escaped, and Cc/Cf/Cs/Co/Cn/Zl/Zp all escaped. The only defect is the data version behind that last test.

HARD CONSTRAINTS RE-CHECKED on the verified snapshot: no `Map`/`WeakMap`/`Set`/`WeakSet` token anywhere in /output; no `require(`; no `module.exports`; every relative import ends in `.mjs`; imports are only node: builtins (node:fs) plus local files; no Python spawned.

divergences.summary: Negative-number matcher is not Unicode-aware. CPython's `_negative_number_matcher = re.compile(r'-\d+$|-\d*\.\d+$')` uses str-mode `\d`, which matches every Unicode category-Nd digit; /output/lib/argparse/parser.mjs:19 uses `/^-\d+$|^-\d*\.\d+$/` where JS `\d` is ASCII-only. So `-١` (U+0661 ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT ONE) is a positional value in the reference but an unknown option in the port, and `--key` then reports a missing argument. Fix: `/^-[\p{Nd}]+$|^-[\p{Nd}]*\.[\p{Nd}]+$/u`. Reproduced with a digit from all 40 Nd blocks tested (Arabic-Indic, Extended Arabic-Indic, NKo, Devanagari, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Oriya, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Sinhala, Thai, Lao, Tibetan, Myanmar, Khmer, Mongolian, Limbu, New Tai Lue, Balinese, Sundanese, Vai, Saurashtra, Kayah Li, Cham, Fullwidth, and astral ones such as U+104A0, U+11066, U+1D7CE, U+1E950). Non-Nd numerics (², ½, ⁵, Ⅰ, ①) correctly do NOT match in either. Also reachable with raw bytes: `--key $'-\xd9\xa1' --val 1`. Forms affected: `-D`, `-DD`, `-.D`, `-D.D`; `-Da` and `-De3` correctly do not match (matcher is fully anchored).

result.notes:
Scope: argparse surface fuzz, black-box only. Nothing under /output or /workspace/dataset was modified; throwaway harnesses live at /tmp/fuzz.mjs, /tmp/fuzz3.mjs, /tmp/fuzz4.mjs, /tmp/probe.mjs, /tmp/raw2.sh, /tmp/fd2.sh, /tmp/fd3.sh.

Case count: 2,353 comparisons, of which ~2,000 are distinct (argv, env, cwd) tuples. Breakdown: 162 from the built-in difftest battery, 810 from /tmp/fuzz.mjs, 914 from /tmp/fuzz3.mjs, 288 from /tmp/fuzz4.mjs, 110 targeted probes, 35 raw-byte argv cases via execve (bypassing Node's UTF-8 argv decoding), and 34 closed-fd / EPIPE / ENOSPC scenarios.

Coverage: missing and duplicated required options; every abbreviation of --key/--val/--help (--k, --ke, --v, --va, --h, --he, --hel) crossed with 8 '=' tails including empty, '==', 'a=b', '=-1', '= '; unknown options; ambiguous prefixes (--, --=, --=x); bare '-', '--', multiple '--' in every gap; interspersed positionals in every gap and gap-pair of the canonical 4-token command; full 4! and 5! ordering permutations; negative-number-lookalikes (-1, -1.5, -0, -00, -.5, -1e3, -1a, -1., -., -1_0, -9999999999999999999999) plus Unicode Nd and non-Nd numerics; short-option-like tokens (-k, -kv, -h, -hh, -hhh, -hx, -hxy, -h=, -h=x, -h-h, -x, -xh); options given as values; values containing '=', spaces, tabs, CR, LF, VT, FF, NBSP, ZWSP, BOM; values up to 20,000 chars and option names up to 4,000 chars; 200-token extras lists; COLUMNS in {1,2,5,9,10,15,19,20,25,33,40,47,48,49,79,80,200,1000,0,-1,abc,''} over the usage/help/error paths; cwd in {/, /tmp, /output, /workspace}; and LC_ALL/LANG/PYTHONIOENCODING/PYTHONWARNINGS variations.

The two argv-reachable findings (Unicode Nd digits; lone-surrogate stderr encoding) are the actionable ones. The five fd findings need shell fd manipulation, which /workspace/verify/difftest.mjs cannot express (it always hands both children fresh pipes), so they will not show up in that harness.

Reference-behaviour notes useful for the fixes: the frozen binary is CPython >= 3.12 argparse — `-hx` appends '-x' to extras and still prints help with exit 0 (3.11 would raise 'ignored explicit argument'), and `-h=` yields "ignored explicit argument ''" rather than the 3.11 IndexError. The port already matches both. The negative-number matcher is the fully-anchored 3.12 form `-\d+$|-\d*\.\d+$` (not 3.13's `-\.?\d`), confirmed because `-1a`, `-1e3` and `-1.` are all classified as unknown options by the reference.

Hard-constraint audit of /output at the time of writing (parser.mjs md5 614cf65580eda1ac25d9bb7f3e6ed283): no Map/WeakMap/Set/WeakSet, no require()/module.exports, every file is .mjs, every relative import carries the .mjs suffix, and the only bare specifier anywhere is 'node:fs'. Note that /output/lib/argparse/parser.mjs changed underneath me mid-session (508 -> 555 lines); all reported divergences were re-confirmed against the current files at the end of the run.
